correctness.rationale: The explicit mean-zero two-terminal Poisson potential is independently checked to solve the correct combinatorial graph Laplacian equation on every part; its edge differences reproduce P. Exhaustive symbolic classification of input edges by selected parts gives S_P=2+(a+b)/N-2R with R=(N-1)(1/(N-a)+1/(N-b))/N. The identity Q=I-P gives S_Q=S_P+1-2R. Score comparisons, factorization of F_2 differences, strict concavity and monotone balanced sums give the exact norms and unique fixed-(N,r) extremizer including boundary cases. The finite exact-rational checker passes 174858 assertions for N<=10 but no infinite claim relies on it.

value.rationale: Bounded edgewise noise amplification of the canonical graph least-squares gradient/circulation split is a structurally motivated operator norm, not the Hilbert norm one. The two complete sharp multipartite norm laws characterize the competing extremal edge types and have distinct optimization behaviors, e.g. the circulation worst edge joins singleton parts for a dominant-part three-block graph. The exact class-wide gradient optimizer and strict limiting amplification constants are useful design and stability benchmarks, not a numerical isolated example.
